no issues, discussions, PRs or bug history before Phase B/C freeze
raw_signal_observation: checkFileChanges shows the same breaking-changes warning when a file version is newer than kFileVersion or older than kBreakingChangesVersion; pressing OK returns the data and permits the open path to continue.
material_claim: The repository proves a deliberate force-open affordance for version-mismatched files, but it does not establish whether newer files should be hard-blocked, whether force-open is an intentional expert escape hatch, or whether opening produces corruption in the deployed product.
neta_next_move: Do not convert version mismatch into a hard block from static source alone. First resolve intended compatibility policy with OWNER; if corruption risk is the deciding claim, reproduce open/save behavior with a pinned newer-version fixture before changing production.
reversal_condition: If explicit maintainer policy or an integrated fixture establishes that newer-version force-open is unsupported and destructive, promote a narrow block or read-only path.
baseline_decision: BUILD: hard-block files with version > kFileVersion to prevent users from opening potentially incompatible data; keep the warning/override only for older migrations.

evidence: Post-freeze issue search for newer/file-version compatibility produced no admissible issue that addresses the exact force-open policy.
Issue #1152 confirms a serious file-loss defect elsewhere in the product, but its Android back-navigation deletion mechanism is unrelated and cannot confirm this compatibility claim.
adjudication.decision_delta: UNRESOLVED: Neta is more restrained than baseline, but no claim-specific external evidence closes whether newer files should be blocked.
adjudication.lesson: A severe neighboring file-loss bug must not be laundered into support for a different compatibility mechanism. HOLDOUT result remains score-only.
